description: The tip is the state after the chain and the work of 2026-11-13 and 2026-11-14. It has the corrections of the optimizer, of the checkers and of the runtime, the new benchmark examples (134 ports of rbenchmark and RBenchmarking in eight categories), `KeyBenchmark`, and the GNU-R fallback of the test interpreter, which gives the optimizer feedback for more of each example. The timed runs of all sections use this commit.
runNotes: The timed runs are from 2026-11-14 to 2026-11-16, on one Mac mini (Apple M4 Pro, 12 cores), with `DEBUG=false` and an R evaluation limit of 600 s. All 30 states were measured again, each with the 134 example files of the tip `56121b617`, because the earlier runs used the old set of examples. For each state, the harness checks out the commit, verifies that the tree is exactly the commit, builds it, times the examples, and compares each benchmark value with GNU-R's. The states `00` to `03` time 85 examples: they cannot compile the other 49. The later states before the tip return a wrong value for 11 examples (9 `fasta` variants, `pidigits`, `mandelbrot_naive_ascii`), which the corrections of the tip repair; no statistic uses these cells. Other work used the machine during the runs (1-minute load average up to 64). The load correction removes the mean effect on a state. The states `05`, `06`, `07`, `14` and `15` had the highest load (load factor 1.05 to 1.13), so they were measured a second time (load factor 0.98 to 1.01), and this report shows the second measurement. The load factor of each state is now 0.96 to 1.08. The two measurements of one state agree within 2% on the geometric mean, but 18 to 35 of the 131 single cells differ by more than 12%. Thus one tinted cell is weak evidence, and a geometric mean is strong evidence. `flexclust` has no time because of the benchmark harness: the timed module runs without the `rsh` package, and only that package installs the hook that gives `body()` of a compiled closure, which S4 `setAs` reads. With `rsh` loaded, the same module runs correctly. The later commit `a1898ff50` corrects the harness; `flexclust` then takes 0.027 s (102% of bc.opt). `pidigits_orbit` has no time at the tip: a speculation on partial feedback deoptimizes, and compiled C cannot deoptimize. In the two tables of variants, hold the pointer on a count or a cell without a time to read the reason. The causes were defects that only a removed optimization shows: `Unbox` unboxed an argument of a dispatch call (a segmentation fault without `optimizeCallee`), `fir2c` called the version of `[<-` that copies the vector in each iteration (the limit of 600 s without `unbox` or `specializeSubscript`), `fir2c` could not compile a builtin call that keeps its closure (no module without `elideBuiltinClosure`), and `SpecializeLocalPromise` failed on a promise without a register (no module without `inline`). The later commits `f2e24be18`, `426d02966`, `6a02b21f2` and `de4c11634` correct them; the tables show the runs of the tip, before these commits. Two causes remain: without `elideTrivialAssume` or `elideUnusedCheckpoints`, a deoptimization block keeps the old vector, so `double_vec_add_t1` and `double_na_vec_add_t1` copy it in each iteration; and a speculation that relies on a removed optimization can deoptimize (`cleaning` without `strictifyPromise`).
